verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a survey on the log-rank conjecture relating deterministic communication complexity to matrix rank, but says nothing about 'local induction rings' or clause-indicator polynomials of CNFs, so it shares vocabulary (rank, communication complexity) without engaging the specific algebraic claim.

verdicts.title: SortNet: Learning To Rank By a Neural-Based Sorting Algorithm
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The problem of relevance ranking consists of sorting a set of objects with respect to a given criterion. Since users may prefer different relevance criteria, the ranking algorithms should be adaptable to the user needs. verdicts.title: The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
The log-rank conjecture is a longstanding open problem with multiple equivalent formulations in complexity theory and mathematics. In its linear-algebraic form, it asserts that the rank and partitioning number of a Boolean matrix are quasi-polynomially related.
